headline: The Pattern Day Trader rule is gone. Intraday margin standards replace it.
the_change: FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-10, published April 20, 2026, retires the long-standing day-trading margin requirements — including the Pattern Day Trader (PDT) framework — and replaces them with new intraday margin standards under Rule 4210. The amendments took effect June 4, 2026, with an 18-month implementation window that runs through October 20, 2027.
why_it_matters: The PDT bright line ($25,000 minimum equity, four-trades-in-five-days counting) is no longer the rule your back office runs on. Firms that built supervisory procedures, alerts, or client disclosures around PDT language now have a stale reference sitting in their compliance manual, and firms without an intraday margin calculation already built into their clearing setup have until October 2027 to get one working.
action_items: Confirm with your clearing firm whether intraday margin calculation is already live on your platform, or whether you're still flagged under the old PDT logic.
Pull every WSP, client agreement, and disclosure that references "pattern day trader" and schedule them for a rewrite — the citation itself is now outdated, not just the mechanics.
Set an internal deadline well inside the 18-month window (e.g., mid-2027) so the transition isn't a scramble in the final quarter.
sifma_note: SIFMA has a long history of commenting on Rule 4210 margin proposals for exactly this kind of implementation detail. Full analysis of any SIFMA response to this specific notice is still pending review — check back as this entry updates.

headline: FINRA wants to modernize the marketing-communications rule — and wants to hear from you first.
the_change: FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-14, issued July 9, 2026, requests comment on proposed changes to modernize Rule 2210, the rule governing communications with the public — the one that touches your website copy, social posts, and pitch decks.
why_it_matters: Rule 2210 changes flow directly into your content-approval workflow. A comment period is the one window where an operational problem you'd actually live with can still get fixed before the rule locks in — after adoption, you're implementing whatever version FINRA finalizes.
action_items: Read Notice 26-14 and flag anything that would break your current marketing-review process, not just the parts that sound significant.
If you want influence on the outcome, submit a comment before the window closes, or at minimum track SIFMA's expected response as a proxy for the industry position.
Hold off on overhauling your content-review process now — comment-period proposals often change materially before adoption.

headline: Most U.S. companies no longer have to file a beneficial ownership report — but keep your file.
the_change: FinCEN's interim final rule, effective March 26, 2025, narrowed the Corporate Transparency Act's "reporting company" definition to cover only entities formed under foreign law that have registered to do business in a U.S. state. Domestic U.S. companies and U.S. persons are no longer required to file beneficial ownership information with FinCEN. A final rule is expected from FinCEN later in 2026, and the underlying statute has not been repealed.
why_it_matters: If you formed a Missouri LLC and either filed a BOI report or were dreading the deadline, you're very likely exempt right now. "Very likely" is doing real work in that sentence — this is an interim rule, not a repeal, and some states have layered on their own transparency filings that this federal rollback doesn't touch.
action_items: Confirm your entity was formed under U.S. law — if so, you're currently exempt from federal BOI reporting.
Keep any beneficial ownership records you already prepared on file rather than discarding them; a 2026 final rule could reinstate a reporting tier.
If you're registered to do business in another state — New York in particular — check that state's own transparency-act deadlines separately; they run on their own clock.

headline: Missouri LLCs don't file an annual report. Corporations do.
the_change: Missouri does not require LLCs to file an annual report with the Secretary of State — no form, no fee, ever. Corporations and nonprofit corporations, by contrast, must file a Registration Report annually or biennially, due by the end of the third month following their registration anniversary date, for $20 online (plus a small processing fee) or $45 by mail.
why_it_matters: Founders who assume every entity type files something every year either miss a corporate registration report they actually owe, or pay a third-party filing service for an LLC "annual report" Missouri never asked for in the first place.
action_items: Confirm your entity type first — LLC vs. corporation changes the answer completely.
If you're a corporation, calendar your registration-report deadline as three months from your registration anniversary, not your fiscal year-end.
If you're an LLC, cancel any recurring "annual report filing" service charging you for something that doesn't exist in Missouri.

headline: FINRA opens comment period on modernizing Rule 5310 best execution guidance
the_change: FINRA issued Regulatory Notice 26-15 seeking public comment on updating its guidance for Rule 5310, the industry standard for best execution. The review follows SEC proposals to eliminate key market structure provisions, including the trade-through rule under Regulation NMS. Comments on the initiative are due by September 25, 2026.
why_it_matters: Changes to Rule 5310 guidance will redefine how firms must evaluate execution quality and document order routing decisions. If federal trade-through protections are rescinded, broker-dealers will need updated FINRA standards to structure compliant, principles-based execution reviews. Small and mid-sized firms will likely face updated expectations for best execution committee oversight and data monitoring.
action_items: Review current Rule 5310 order-routing procedures and execution quality documentation.
Identify how potential SEC changes to Regulation NMS would impact your order-handling workflows.
Submit feedback to FINRA prior to the September 25, 2026 comment deadline.
Confirm with counsel how this specific change applies to your situation.

headline: FINRA Proposes Replacing Mandatory Pre-Approval for Retail Communications
the_change: FINRA issued Regulatory Notice 26-14 proposing to eliminate mandatory principal pre-use approval for retail communications under Rule 2210. The proposal replaces rigid pre-approval with risk-based supervisory standards designed for modern channels like social media and generative AI. Public comments on the proposed framework are due by September 11, 2026.
why_it_matters: Routine compliance bottlenecks on low-risk marketing content will disappear for broker-dealers. Replacing automatic pre-approval shifts compliance burden from administrative pre-clearing to substantive supervisory testing and post-use auditing.
action_items: Map your existing communication pre-approval workflows to identify routine content eligible for risk-based post-use review.
Assess whether your current compliance systems can effectively monitor and archive AI-generated marketing content.
Submit comments on Regulatory Notice 26-14 before the September 11, 2026 deadline.
